quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Have to' sounds like one chunk when spoken — don't expect a pause between the two words.
quests.explanation: Subject (I) + 'have to' (obligation) + verb (finish) + object (this report) + time (today). 'Have to' expresses a duty coming from outside, like a deadline.
quests.textToSpeak: I have to finish this report today.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: With 'she', 'have' changes to 'has' — the same rule as present simple verbs.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + 'has to' + verb (catch) + object (an early train). Third-person singular subjects need 'has to', not 'have to'.
quests.textToSpeak: She has to catch an early train.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'Soon' closes the sentence, showing the deadline isn't immediate but is approaching.
quests.explanation: Subject (We) + 'have to' + verb (renew) + object (our passports) + time (soon). 'Soon' suggests urgency without giving an exact date.
quests.textToSpeak: We have to renew our passports soon.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Must' is stronger than 'have to' and often signals a fixed rule, not a personal choice.
quests.explanation: Subject (You) + 'must' + base verb (wear) + object (a seatbelt) + place (here). 'Must' expresses a rule the speaker considers non-negotiable.
quests.textToSpeak: You must wear a seatbelt here.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Mustn't' means something is forbidden — very different in meaning from 'don't have to'.
quests.explanation: Subject (Visitors) + 'mustn't' (prohibition) + verb (touch) + object (the artwork). 'Mustn't' forbids an action completely, unlike a weaker suggestion.
quests.textToSpeak: Visitors mustn't touch the artwork.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'By nine' means no later than that time — listen for the deadline word 'by'.
quests.explanation: Subject (Employees) + 'must' + verb phrase (clock in) + deadline (by nine). 'By' marks the latest acceptable time for an action.
quests.textToSpeak: Employees must clock in by nine.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Should' offers advice, softer than 'must' — listen for that gentler tone in the structure.
quests.explanation: Subject (You) + 'should' (advice) + verb (drink) + quantity (more water) + frequency (daily). 'Should' recommends without forcing.
quests.textToSpeak: You should drink more water daily.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Again' tells us this has happened before and shouldn't repeat.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + 'shouldn't' + verb (skip) + object (his medication) + 'again'. Negative advice with 'shouldn't' warns against repeating a mistake.
quests.textToSpeak: He shouldn't skip his medication again.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: A small time clause trails at the end, explaining when to act.
quests.explanation: Subject (We) + 'should' + verb (leave) + time clause (before the traffic starts). 'Before' introduces the later event we want to avoid.
quests.textToSpeak: We should leave before the traffic starts.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Would like to' is a polite, formal way of saying 'want to' — all three words stay together.
quests.explanation: Subject (I) + 'would like to' + verb (order) + object (the soup). This phrase is more polite than simply saying 'I want'.
quests.textToSpeak: I would like to order the soup.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: As an offer, the whole phrase flips to the front, before the subject.
quests.explanation: 'Would' + subject (you) + 'like' + quantity (some more) + object (tea)? This word order turns a statement into a polite offer.
quests.textToSpeak: Would you like some more tea?

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'She'd' packs 'she' and 'would' into one quick sound at the start.
quests.explanation: 'She'd' (She + would) + 'like to' + verb (change) + object (her appointment). Spoken English often contracts 'would' onto the subject like this.
quests.textToSpeak: She'd like to change her appointment.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Need to' behaves just like 'have to' — a verb glued to 'to' before the action.
quests.explanation: Subject (I) + 'need to' + verb (renew) + object (my library card). Verbs like 'need' are often followed by 'to' plus another verb.
quests.textToSpeak: I need to renew my library card.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Plan to' introduces a future intention, not something happening right now.
quests.explanation: Subject (They) + 'plan to' + verb (open) + object (a new branch). 'Plan to' expresses an intention decided in advance.
quests.textToSpeak: They plan to open a new branch.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: The main verb is past tense, but the second verb after 'to' stays in its base form.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + verb (decided) + 'to' + base verb (learn) + object (a new skill). Even after a past-tense verb, 'to' is followed by the base form.
quests.textToSpeak: He decided to learn a new skill.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Enjoy' is followed by an '-ing' form, not 'to' plus a verb.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + verb (enjoys) + gerund (hiking) + time (on weekends). Verbs like 'enjoy' take an '-ing' form directly after them.
quests.textToSpeak: She enjoys hiking on weekends.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: Same pattern as 'enjoy' — 'avoid' also pulls in the '-ing' form right after it.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + verb (avoids) + gerund (eating) + time (late at night). 'Avoid' never takes 'to' — only the '-ing' form follows it.
quests.textToSpeak: He avoids eating late at night.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: This polite question uses 'mind' plus '-ing', not 'mind to' — a common learner mistake to avoid.
quests.explanation: 'Do' + subject (you) + verb (mind) + gerund (opening) + object (the window)? 'Mind' as a polite request always takes the '-ing' form.
quests.textToSpeak: Do you mind opening the window?

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Let's' proposes a shared action — it opens the sentence like a friendly command.
quests.explanation: 'Let's' (Let us) + verb (grab) + object (lunch) + time (before the meeting). 'Let's' suggests doing something together.
quests.textToSpeak: Let's grab lunch before the meeting.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Or' offers a choice between two options — listen for which one comes first.
quests.explanation: Subject (You) + 'can' + verb (pay) + method 1 (by card) + 'or' + method 2 (cash). 'Or' connects two alternative choices.
quests.textToSpeak: You can pay by card or cash.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'Why not' is another way to suggest something, different from 'let's' but with the same friendly purpose.
quests.explanation: 'Why not' + base verb (take) + object (the stairs) + 'instead of' + alternative (the elevator)? 'Why not' politely suggests an alternative option.
quests.textToSpeak: Why not take the stairs instead of the elevator?

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'That' introduces a second, smaller sentence hiding inside the first one.
quests.explanation: Subject (I) + verb (think) + 'that' + embedded clause (the plan will work). 'That' connects an opinion verb to the idea being expressed.
quests.textToSpeak: I think that the plan will work.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: The embedded clause has its own subject and verb, just like a mini sentence.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + verb (believes) + 'that' + embedded clause (honesty matters most). Embedded clauses can be dropped into larger sentences after opinion verbs.
quests.textToSpeak: She believes that honesty matters most.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'Stays' — not 'stay' — because the embedded subject 'the weather' is singular.
quests.explanation: Subject (We) + verb (hope) + 'that' + embedded clause (the weather stays clear). The embedded verb still agrees with its own subject inside the clause.
quests.textToSpeak: We hope that the weather stays clear.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Yet' works like 'but', joining a strength with an unexpected downside.
quests.explanation: Clause 1 (The app is fast) + 'yet' + clause 2 (it drains the battery). 'Yet' introduces a surprising contrast, similar in meaning to 'but'.
quests.textToSpeak: The app is fast, yet it drains the battery.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: Two different actions are offered as choices, joined by 'or'.
quests.explanation: Subject (You) + 'can' + option 1 (email me) + 'or' + option 2 (call the office). Coordinated verb phrases can each carry a different object.
quests.textToSpeak: You can email me or call the office.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'As well as' adds a second item without repeating the verb — listen for what follows it.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + verb (manages) + object 1 (the budget) + 'as well as' + object 2 (the schedule). 'As well as' means 'in addition to'.
quests.textToSpeak: She manages the budget as well as the schedule.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: Two structures from this file combine: obligation first, then an embedded opinion.
quests.explanation: Clause 1 (I have to leave early) + 'because' + clause 2 (I think the traffic will be bad). An obligation and its embedded reasoning can share one sentence.
quests.textToSpeak: I have to leave early because I think the traffic will be bad.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'So' introduces the purpose of the advice — why calling ahead actually helps.
quests.explanation: Clause 1 (We should call ahead) + 'so' (purpose) + clause 2 (they know we're coming). 'So' here explains the goal behind the suggested action.
quests.textToSpeak: We should call ahead so they know we're coming.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: A polite wish and a real obligation are balanced against each other with 'but'.
quests.explanation: Clause 1 (She'd like to visit soon) + 'but' + clause 2 (she has to finish her project first). 'But' weighs a wish against a current responsibility.
quests.textToSpeak: She'd like to visit soon, but she has to finish her project first.
